In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Commentary on Surah al-Falaq

It is a Meccan surah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾. On this there are several opinions. The first, and it is the most apparent: that al-falaq (the daybreak) is the dawn, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿He is the Cleaver of the daybreak﴾. The second opinion: that it is the whole of creation. The third opinion: that it is a house in the Fire, which, when its door is opened, the people of Hell cry out because of its intense heat; this was said by Ka'b al-Ahbar. The fourth opinion: that it is a pit in Hell; this was said by Mujahid.
And His saying: ﴿From the evil of what He created﴾ means: from the evil of all that He created.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 113, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾ — there are also other opinions regarding it. One of them: "From the evil of the night when it becomes dark." So al-Ghasiq (the darkness) is the night. This was said by al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah. It is also said: "From the evil of the night when it approaches."

It is said: waqaba means "entered," and it was said "approached." The meaning of seeking refuge from the night is that in it the stirring of worries occurs, and every person of evil attacks with intent.

The second opinion: His saying ﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾ refers to the moon. There is a well-known report on this, narrated by Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand, pointed to the moon, and said: 'Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for it is the darkness when it settles.'"

Abu 'Isa (al-Tirmidhi) mentioned it in his Jami' and said: "It is a sound hadith (hadith sahih)."

al-Nahhas said: It is permissible that the seeking of refuge be from the moon, because some people associated partners with Allah through it, so the seeking of refuge is attributed to it metaphorically.

al-Qutaybi said: ﴿From the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾ is the moon when it enters its shahur, i.e., its covering, and that is when it sets.

Some of them mentioned that seeking refuge is from the moon because the people of the earth watch for the face of the moon, i.e., its setting, and they are thieves and people of evil and corruption. The third opinion: al-Ghasiq is the Pleiades (al-Thurayya).

His saying ﴿when it settles﴾ means when it sets. It was mentioned that when the Pleiades set, afflictions and calamities appear, and when the Pleiades rise, afflictions and calamities are lifted.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the star rises, the affliction is lifted from every land."

This includes plague, pestilence, diseases and what resembles them.

It was also said: "From the evil of the darkness when it settles" means from the evil of the sun when it sets.

al-Naqqash mentioned, with his chain of narration, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "From the evil of the darkness when it settles: from the evil of the male organ when it enters." al-Naqqash said: "I mentioned that to Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah and said: 'Is it permissible to interpret the Qur'an in this way?' He said: 'Yes, the Prophet said: "I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing..."' — a well-known report — and he said: 'I seek refuge in You from the evil of my semen (manyi).'" (The Prophet listed several things, and at the end said: "...and from the evil of my semen.")
And His saying: ﴿And from the evil of those who blow upon knots﴾, i.e., the sorceresses. Al-nafth (blowing) is blowing with the mouth, and al-tafl (spitting) is when it is accompanied by saliva.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 113, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿And from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾. Al-hasad (envy) is wishing for the removal of the blessing from the one upon whom it has been bestowed. We have already mentioned some matters concerning envy earlier. It has also been said: "from the evil of an envier when he envies" means: when he oppresses.

Know that the exegetes said: this surah and the one that follows it were revealed when the Prophet was bewitched; he was bewitched by Labid ibn A'sam, a Jew.

As for ﴿the blowers in knots﴾, it is said that they are his daughters.

Labid had bewitched the Prophet and placed it in a well (Dhi Arwan). The Prophet fell ill, and his illness grew severe, and he would imagine that he was doing something when he was not doing it. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatan).

It is narrated that he said to A'ishah: "While I was sleeping, two angels came down to me. One of them sat at my head and the other at my feet. One said to his companion: 'What is the matter with the man?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.' He asked: 'And who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn A'sam, the Jew.' He asked: 'And where is it?' He said: 'In a comb and combings, under a spathe of a date palm, in the well of Dhi Arwan.' Then the Prophet sent to us [people] (it is said he sent Ammar, and it is said he sent Abu Bakr and Umar) until they extracted that sorcery. Allah the Exalted sent down these two surahs. On that object there were eleven knots. Jibril said to him: 'Recite a verse,' and a knot came undone; whenever he recited a verse, a knot came undone, until all the knots were undone. The Prophet rose as if he had been released from a tether."
